title: Bacteria and Prokaryotic Life
text: Bacteria are prokaryotic microorganisms that lack a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. They are among the most numerous and diverse organisms on Earth, found in virtually every environment. Bacteria play crucial roles in nutrient cycling, decomposition, and nitrogen fixation in ecosystems. Some bacteria are pathogenic and cause diseases such as tuberculosis, cholera, and pneumonia. The human body contains approximately as many bacterial cells as human cells, with the gut microbiome playing an important role in digestion and immune function. Bacteria are generally classified by their shape (cocci, bacilli, spirilla), Gram stain reaction, and metabolic characteristics.
